## Bug-Introducing Commits
BIC: 893eb1eeda39303b9ce5eb81a050de64e56d67fb

## Reasoning

**(1) Investigation:** The fix commit changes `addBootCP` in `Options.java` from `bootclasspathDirectories().addAll(value)` to `bootclasspathDirectories().addAll(0, value)` — i.e., from appending to prepending. I used `git log --follow -p` on `Options.java` to trace every historical change to `addBootCP`/`bootclasspathDirectories`, and found several intervening commits that only refactored field access into accessor methods (e.g. `6bba0b3b`) or changed casting style (`b750dafb`), none of which altered the append-vs-prepend semantics. I then traced back to the commit that first introduced the `addBootCP` method itself.

**(2) The originating change:** Commit `893eb1eeda39303b9ce5eb81a050de64e56d67fb` ("Owen Arden", 2012-07-25) introduced the `-addbootcp` flag and its handler `addBootCP(List<File> value)`, implemented as:
```java
protected void addBootCP(List<File> value) {
    bootclasspath_directories.addAll(value);
}
```
This appends to the end of the list instead of inserting at the front.

**(3) Supporting evidence:** In the very same commit, the flag was declared with the description:
```java
flags.add(new PathFlag<File>("-addbootcp", "<path>",
        "prepend <path> to the bootclasspath") { ... });
```
The flag's own documentation says "prepend", but the implementation from day one used `addAll(value)` (append), not `addAll(0, value)` (prepend) — a direct contradiction between stated intent and actual behavior. A search of the entire history (`git log --all -S"addbootcp"`) shows this string/feature appears in only this one commit, confirming there is no earlier "correct" version that later regressed — the bug was present from the feature's introduction. All later commits touching this code were pure refactors (splitting fields into accessor methods, changing cast helpers) and preserved the same (buggy) append behavior until the 2016 fix commit corrected it to match the documented "prepend" semantics.

I'm highly confident in this identification, since the string search (`-S"addbootcp"`) definitively shows only one commit ever introduced this code path, and that commit's own flag description reveals the intended behavior being violated.
